The ASV writes no presentative frame for הָיָה at all — no *it shall come to pass* stands in the verse — so nothing realizes this verb. Rule 45 gives a הָיָה the complementizer of a frame the ASV has written; with the frame absent, the *that* answers to the לְ of the recast infinitive clause instead. Corrected from the accepted reading, which aligned הָיָה to the bare *that*.

לְ + infinitive construct recast as a finite clause: the preposition takes the complementizer *that* while the infinitive keeps its supplied modal and lexical verb (rule 52, settled in 28 corpus units and never placed on the infinitive). The competing reading gives the *that* to the presentative הָיָה under rule 45.
Infinitive keeps the supplied modal and the lexical verb (rule 52).

review_notes: Corrected: the single *that* moves from הָיָה to the לְ of לָנוּס. Rule 45's complementizer belongs to a presentative frame the ASV has actually written, and this verse writes none; rule 52's finite recasting of לְ + infinitive (*that … may flee*) is the construction the ASV did write, and it puts the complementizer on the preposition. הָיָה and its waw are both left unrepresented.

The assimilated article takes the quantifying determiner *any* written in its place, standing where the phrase's *the* would stand (rule 41: `הַבֶּגֶד` → *any garment*). No other morpheme licenses that word — no כֹּל stands in the phrase and the demonstrative is already answered by *such* — and rule 15 gives a supplied *any* to the noun only where no determiner morpheme stands before the word it determines. Corrected from the accepted reading, which marked this article unrepresented and made *any* the whole rendering of דָּבָר.

Generic head noun דָּבָר with the attributive that names the class rendered by the one English word *evil*, which carries both senses; the pair shares a unit headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme (rule 30's generic-noun sentence, `אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה` → *harlot's*, which forbids marking the generic unrepresented beside it). The competing reading leaves דָּבָר unrepresented and gives *evil* to רָע alone.

review_notes: Corrected in the phrase *any such evil*. The assimilated article of כַּדָּבָר is a determiner morpheme standing before the word it determines, so rule 41 gives it the quantifying *any* and rule 15's supplied-determiner sentence does not reach the noun; the accepted alignment had marked that article unrepresented and aligned דָּבָר to *any* on the premise that nothing else in the phrase licensed the word.

With *any* placed on the article, דָּבָר and רָע are read as rule 30's generic head noun plus class-naming attributive rendered by the one word *evil*, headed on רָע, rather than leaving the generic noun unrepresented beside it.
